act: CSS Cascading and Inheritance Level 6 (Editor's Draft, 28 April 2026)

en.title: CSS Cascade 6: §3.5.1 says scope proximity wins regardless of specificity, while §3.1 compares specificity first
en.summary: §3.5.1 of the Editor's Draft says the cascade prefers the more proximate scoping root “regardless of specificity”. §3.1 lists Specificity before Scope Proximity, and the changes list records “Removed strong scope proximity” after the Working Group resolved in issue 6790 that proximity is weaker than specificity. The §3.5.1 sentence still describes the old rule; the Working Draft of 6 September 2024 has the same sentence.
en.impact: #page img { border-radius: 0 } (specificity 1,0,1) against @scope (#hero) { img { border-radius: 50% } } (0,0,1) for an image inside #hero: by §3.1 the radius is 0, by the §3.5.1 sentence it is 50%.
en.correction: Reword the §3.5.1 sentence to match §3.1: proximity decides only when all earlier cascade criteria tie.

quotes.source: CSS Cascading and Inheritance Level 6, Editor's Draft of 28 April 2026 (W3C CSS Working Group)
quotes.text: The cascade prioritizes declarations with a more proximate scoping root, regardless of specificity or order of appearance by applying scope proximity between the scoping root and the subject of each scoped style rule.

quotes.source: CSS Cascading and Inheritance Level 6, Editor's Draft of 28 April 2026 (W3C CSS Working Group)
quotes.text: When comparing declarations from two style rules, the declaration belonging to the style rule with the highest specificity wins.
